questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

On the ball

options.text: Unaware of any changes or developments and lazy to react to them
Aware of any changes or developments but slow to react to them
Aware of any changes or developments and quick to react to them
Aware of any changes or developments but doing nothing

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"on the ball"** means being aware of any changes or developments and quick to react to them. (जागरूक और तत्पर)

 
 
• **Example: **She is always **on the ball **and never misses a deadline.
 
 
 
• **Explanation:** The idiom indicates someone who is quick to understand and react in a situation, showing alertness and efficiency. (जागरूकता और कुशलता दिखाना)
 
 
• **Example: **Our new manager is really **on the ball** when it comes to handling customer complaints.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: Unaware of any changes or developments and lazy to react to them** (परिवर्तनों या विकासों से अनजान और प्रतिक्रिया करने में आलसी)

 
 
• **Example:** He missed the opportunity because he was unaware of any changes or developments and lazy to react to them.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Aware of any changes or developments but slow to react to them** (परिवर्तनों या विकासों से अवगत लेकिन प्रतिक्रिया करने में धीमा)
 
 
• **Example:** Though he knew about the changes, he was aware of any changes or developments but slow to react to them.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Aware of any changes or developments but doing nothing** (परिवर्तनों या विकासों से अवगत लेकिन कुछ नहीं करना)
 
 
• **Example:** She was aware of any changes or developments but doing nothing, leading to missed opportunities.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

I have been living in Hyderabad __since I am born__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the present tense** "am" after "since." **The correct** past tense form should be used.**
 
• The correct phrase should be **"since I was born,"** ensuring **grammatical correctness and clarity.**
 
• The use of** "since" **indicates a point in time from the past until now, requiring the past tense "was" to be grammatically correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I have been living in Hyderabad** since I was born."***

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "since I have born,"** – Incorrect because "have born" is not a correct tense form.
 
• **Option 2: "since I will be born,"** – Incorrect because "will be born" indicates future tense, which is not applicable here.
 
• **Option 3: "since I born,"** – Incorrect because "born" without "was" is grammatically incorrect.

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. More children go to school than at any time in the past. But more children today are out of school than any time in the past.

B. But it is not enough to blame the high birth rate for this state of affairs.

C. Indeed, it can be reasonably argued that continued mass illiteracy is not the result but the cause of the high birth rate.

D. There are more literate people in India today than ever before. But there are also more illiterates than ever before.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph** begins **by introducing the central concept of literacy and illiteracy in India, setting a contrasting tone regarding the existence of both more literate and illiterate people today: **Sentence D**.
 
• **Sentence A** follows,** providing** a specific example of the paradoxical situation in today's context, more children attending school yet also more children out of school: "More children go to school than at any time in the past. But more children today are out of school than any time in the past."
 
• **Sentence B** **continues **by stating that it is not sufficient to blame only the high birth rate for this situation: "But it is not enough to blame the high birth rate for this state of affairs."
 
• **Sentence C** **concludes** the argument by presenting the idea that illiteracy may actually be the cause of the high birth rate rather than the effect: "Indeed, it can be reasonably argued that continued mass illiteracy is not the result but the cause of the high birth rate."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Rearranged Paragraph:** *"There are more literate people in India today than ever before. But there are also more illiterates than ever before. More children go to school than at any time in the past. But more children today are out of school than any time in the past. But it is not enough to blame the high birth rate for this state of affairs. Indeed, it can be reasonably argued that continued mass illiteracy is not the result but the cause of the high birth rate."*

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The contract was grabbed by the biggest telecom company in India.

options.text: The biggest telecom company in India grabbed the contract.
The biggest telecom company in India grabs the contract.
The biggest telecom company in India will grab the contract.
The biggest telecom company in India has grabbed the contract.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the** passive voice** and **needs to be converted to the active voice.**
 
• In the passive voice, the subject receives the action, **whereas**, in the active voice, the subject performs the action.
 
• The correct active voice sentence should identify the doer of the action first, followed by the action itself.
 
• Thus, the correct active voice sentence is: **"The biggest telecom company in India grabbed the contract."**

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The biggest telecom company in India grabbed the contract."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "The biggest telecom company in India grabs the contract."** – This is in the present tense, while the original sentence is in the past tense.
 
• **Option 3: "The biggest telecom company in India will grab the contract."** – This is in the future tense, which does not match the original sentence's past tense.
 
• **Option 4: "The biggest telecom company in India has grabbed the contract."** – This is in the present perfect tense, which does not match the original sentence's past tense.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

By whom was grammar taught to you?

options.text: You were taught grammar by whom?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence** "By whom was grammar taught to you?"** is in** the passive voice**.
 
• To express it in the active voice, we need to identify the subject performing the action (who) and place it at the beginning of the sentence.
 
• The structure in active voice would be **"Who taught you grammar?"**
 
• In this construction,** "who"** is the subject,** "taught"** is the verb, and** "you"** is the object.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Who taught you grammar?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"Did he teach you grammar?" - This is a yes/no question but does not use the correct subject "who" or the correct structure.
 
• **Option 2: **"Who had taught you grammar?" - Incorrect tense (past perfect instead of simple past).
 
• **Option 3: **"You were taught grammar by whom?" - This is in the passive voice and merely rephrases the original question without changing the voice.
